Suppose that $x$ is a real number. The least integer (or ceiling) function $⌈x⌉$ equals the smallest integer that is greater than or equal to $x:$ 

$$
⌈x⌉=n,\,\text{where}\,n-1<x\le n,\,n\in Z
$$

From the definition of the least integer function, we have

$$
⌈-4⌉=-4.
$$

The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨f(t),f(t)⟩}.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }(f(t))^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }\,{cos}^{2}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }(\frac{1+\operatorname{cos}⁡2t}{2})\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡2t}{2})\,\text{d}t \\  & =(\frac{t}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡2t}{4}){|}_{\pi }^{2\pi } \\  & =(\frac{2\pi }{2}+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡4\pi }{4})-(\frac{\pi }{2}+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\pi }{4}) \\  & =(\pi +0)-(\frac{\pi }{2}+0) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we made use of the trigonometric identity 

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡t=\frac{1+\operatorname{cos}⁡2t}{2}.
$$

Finally then,

$$
\begin{aligned}‖f(t)‖ & =\sqrt{\frac{\pi }{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

A first-order linear system of differential equations with two dependent variables is a system of equations that takes the following standard form:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=a(t){x}_{1}(t)+b(t){x}_{2}(t)+f(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=c(t){x}_{1}(t)+d(t){x}_{2}(t)+g(t)\end{aligned}
$$

where

- $a(t),$ $b(t),$ $c(t),$ $d(t),$ $f(t),$ and $g(t)$ are known functions, and

- ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ are unknown functions (dependent variables).

Such a system can always be written in the form

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+f(t)
$$

where

$$
x(t)=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}a(t) & b(t) \\ c(t) & d(t)\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}f(t) \\ g(t)\end{aligned}].
$$

We have the following system.

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)-2{x}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}(t)=0 \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)+8{x}_{1}(t)=0\end{aligned}
$$

Writing our system in standard form, we get the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=2{x}_{1}(t)-{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-8{x}_{1}(t)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can rewrite our system in matrix form as follows:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -8 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t)
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -8 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$
